title: Activation-mix hyperprofile orchestrator for INT8 calibration and runtime kernel routing
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Build an 'activation-mix hyperprofile' component that produces per-model and per-workload INT8 calibration profiles (activation/weight scale mixes) and exposes runtime routing rules so the inference engine can pick the best kernel and profile at request time. Background: several models with KV-cache heavy patterns show non-uniform activation distributions across layers and prompt sizes; a single static scale per-layer causes either accuracy regressions or excessive headroom. Goals: 1) Produce concise calibration profiles that capture activation distribution mix (percentile and second-order moments) per layer and per sequence-length bucket. 2) Provide an orchestrator service that stores profiles, exposes a compact runtime lookup API, and publishes kernel-routing hints for the serving runtime (fused-kernel vs fallback, per-device). 3) Add validation harnesses that quantify end-to-end generation/beam accuracy regressions vs FP16 and produce per-profile acceptance metrics. Out of scope: FP8 prototype and full per-channel retraining. Approach: - Calibration harness will run representative prompt sets across sequence lengths and batch patterns, collecting activation histograms and per-layer moments. - A profile compressor will convert histograms to a small hyperprofile (layer band, percentile thresholds, activation-to-weight scale ratio recommendation). - The orchestrator will store profiles keyed by model-id, sequence-length-bucket, and workload-tag; it will also compute runtime routing rules (e.g., prefer fused INT8 kernels if activation skew < threshold; otherwise use per-layer compensator + fallback kernels). - The runtime runtime-agent will fetch profile at model load and subscribe to changes; the serving kernel selector will consider profile hints alongside device capabilities. - Validation: run end-to-end generation comparisons (ROUGE/BLEU/embedding-similarity + model-specific evals) and fail profile rollout if accuracy drop exceeds engineered thresholds. Success criteria: shipping a profile format and orchestrator API, runtime kernel selection integration, and a regression dashboard for top-10 models.
acceptance_criteria: Hyperprofile file format v1 documented and < 3KB per profile for 7B models
Orchestrator API: GET /profiles?model={id}&seq_bucket={n} returns profile and kernel_hints
Runtime agent fetch + subscription integrated into serving runtime with <5ms cold load overhead
Kernel selector uses profile hints and falls back cleanly with no crash/onboarding errors
Evaluation harness measures generation quality and flags regressions >0.8% embedding-sim drop or >1.5% token-level perf drop
End-to-end tests in CI covering fused vs fallback kernels with selected profiles
implementation_tasks: Calibration harness: add sequence-bucketed activation collector (ENG branch: quant/hyperprof)
Profile compressor: implement percentile extractor + delta encoding
Orchestrator service: store profiles, simple UI to inspect profile per model
Runtime agent: fetch/subscribe implementation + integration test
Kernel selector: accept profile hints and route to fused/compensator kernels
Validation harness: generation comparison scripts, threshold alerts, dashboard ingest
CI: add regression job that runs top-5 release models with new profiles
test_plan: Unit tests for percentile extractor and compressor (coverage > 90%)
Integration test: profile round-trip orchestrator <-> runtime agent
Perf test: measure serving latency and cold-start overhead with profile fetch (target <5ms)
Quality test: run evaluation prompts and compare against FP16 baseline; record embedding and token-level metrics
Staging rollout: Canary profiles on dedicated pool with automatic rollback on metric breach
risks_mitigation: Risk: Over-compressed profiles miss tail behavior -> Mitigation: keep a reserve mode with raw histograms for models that fail validation
Risk: Runtime fetch adds latency burst -> Mitigation: cache profiles in persistent local store + prefetch during model load
Risk: Kernel mismatch across device types -> Mitigation: include device capability tags and add conservative fallback hints
Risk: Evaluation thresholds not reflective of user-facing quality -> Mitigation: include production prompt-snapshots for top customers in validation
